Article Title: As gold falls from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, Indians buy 30% more, spending Rs 72,000 crore on 52 tonnes; silver demand rises 10%
Article Text:
In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%.

Gold price correction from Rs 1.8 lakh peak

Gold generates big returns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.The industry body estimated that consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.The increase followed a correction in gold prices from a peak of around Rs 1.8 lakh to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, drawing buyers back into the market. Purchases made in advance of the wedding season, which starts in mid-November and runs until March, also helped boost demand.“Jewellers have made good business in this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali,” IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET.Mehta said the market was witnessing pent-up demand, as several consumers had put off buying gold after Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people not to purchase the metal.“Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing .”The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses.“This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment,” said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council.In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%. The fall was attributed to higher prices, an increase in import duty and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to consumers to refrain from buying gold.Despite the volatility, gold has generated significant returns over the past few years. Prices, which were around Rs 60,000 per 10 grams in 2023, climbed to Rs 80,000 in 2024 and reached Rs 1.15 lakh-Rs 1.20 lakh in 2025. During this year’s Dhanteras-Diwali period, prices stood at approximately Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver has also recorded a substantial appreciation in value.An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers found that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third-highest in a decade, even though prices were around 10% above their level a year earlier.“The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period,” said C Vinod Hayagriv, director of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers.Natural diamonds also held up well, registering their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer recorded a 250% increase in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras, while sales during the Diwali season rose 47%.The performance comes at a time when the natural diamond industry is facing disruption from global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and increasing competition from lab-grown alternatives. However, lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional product category rather than displacing natural diamonds.
Article Summary: Indian consumers increased their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year. Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.

Article Title: Nvidia loses $500 billion since last week amid 'spy' scandal; Jensen Huang slips to 13th on Forbes rich list
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after reports came out on multiple affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers.Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.Also read: Trump unsure woman linked to Jensen Huang was a spy; report alleges 3rd affair of ex-Nvidia CEO The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19. The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.

Article Title: Mother Dairy, Amul milk gets costlier: Dairy giant hikes rate by upto Rs 6 per litre from Thursday; check prices
Article Text:
Mother Dairy raises prices

Why are milk prices increasing?

How much will milk cost now?

Full cream milk (packaged): Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72.

Nandini had also raised milk prices in Karnataka

NEW DELHI: Milk is set to get costlier in Delhi NCR from November 12, with dairy companies Mother Dairy and Amul increasing prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. The price hike comes amid lower milk supplies and higher costs of buying milk from farmers.The increase will vary across milk varieties. Toned milk will cost Rs 2 more per litre, full cream milk Rs 4 more and full cream buffalo milk Rs 6 more, according to industry sources.In Delhi-NCR, full cream packaged milk will now cost Rs 76 per litre, compared with Rs 72 earlier. Packaged toned milk will cost Rs 62, up from Rs 60, while toned milk sold through bulk vending machines will cost Rs 60 against Rs 58 earlier.Double-toned milk will become costlier from Rs 54 to Rs 56 per litre. Cow milk prices will rise from Rs 62 to Rs 65, while full cream buffalo milk, which contains 6.5% fat, will cost Rs 86 against Rs 80 earlier.Mother Dairy, the largest milk supplier in Delhi-NCR, had last increased prices on May 14, 2026.Milk procurement has become more expensive for dairy companies. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs.Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve. The shortage has affected the availability of milk fat, making it more expensive for dairy companies.When fresh milk supplies fall short, companies usually use milk powder and milk fat to prepare liquid milk. However, higher milk fat prices have also increased the cost of this process.Dairy companies have raised the prices they pay farmers to encourage them to produce and supply more milk. Amul has increased the procurement rate linked to milk fat to Rs 1,000 per kilogram. This allows farmers to receive more than Rs 60 per litre for milk, according to industry sources.Mother Dairy has decided to pass on part of these higher costs to consumers. The company pays farmers 75-80% of the money it earns from milk sales, sources told PTI.Here are the revised prices of different milk varieties in Delhi-NCR:Mother Dairy sells around 35 lakh litres of milk every day in Delhi-NCR through its outlets, general trade and e-commerce platforms. Its total daily milk sales across markets exceed 50 lakh litres.The company reported a 17% rise in turnover to Rs 20,300 crore in the last fiscal year. The growth was driven by higher demand for its milk products and cooking oils.Started in 1974, Mother Dairy is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). It sells milk and milk products under the Mother Dairy brand, edible oils under Dhara, and fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen vegetables, snacks, pulps and concentrates under Safal.Before the latest increase by Mother Dairy and Amul, Nandini had raised milk prices in Karnataka. The state Cabinet approved an Rs 8 per litre increase in the base price, with the new rates taking effect from November 1.The Karnataka government said the increase was needed to protect dairy farmers facing severe drought conditions. Law and parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the revised prices were still within the range charged in most other states.He also said rising prices of other goods had hurt farmers and milk supply in Karnataka had fallen by 10 lakh litres due to the drought this year.Cooperation minister Laxman Savadi said the government also had to consider the possibility of farmers selling their milk to other states if prices were not increased. This could have led to a shortage of milk in Karnataka.Under the revised arrangement, Rs 7 of the Rs 8 per litre increase was to go to farmers, while Re 1 was allocated to milk unions in the state.
Article Summary: Mother Dairy and Amul increase prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs. Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve.

Article Title: US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US operations
Article Text:
Air India warns of disruptions to flights to and from America

Network router problem suspected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India flights operating to and from the US could face disruptions after a communication outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a nationwide ground stop on departures.The airline said the disruption had affected departures from airports across the country, potentially impacting its US operations. It has advised passengers to check their flight status before setting out for the airport and plan their travel accordingly."A nationwide ground stop is currently in effect across the US due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. As a result, departures from airports across US are impacted, with possible consequential disruptions to Air India flights to and from the US," the airline wrote on X.Air India said its teams were monitoring the situation closely and would provide further updates as they became available.However, the ground stop has now been lifted according to Reuters, but the disruption is likely to continue.The chaos follows the FAA's had halted departures across the country on Friday after a telecommunications outage affected regional air traffic control operations. The restriction brought departures to a standstill at airports across the US, leaving thousands of passengers facing disrupted travel plans.The FAA said the decision was taken "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".The outage affected all 22 regional air route traffic control centres, which direct aircraft travelling between airports. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said FAA technicians were investigating the problem, while the agency maintained that the communication disruption made it unsafe for flights to continue departing normally.Also Read| US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so far The precise cause of the outage remained under investigation. However, according to an airline source cited by CNN, the FAA informed carriers that a problem with network routers had triggered the disruption. The issue was believed to have started at Chicago Midway International Airport before spreading across the country.During initial crisis discussions, the FAA was reportedly unable to give a clear explanation of the problem. Different facilities were experiencing the outage in different ways.Homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said the problem appeared to be related to telecommunications. Officials had no indication that it was the result of an attack, although authorities were examining the communication systems used by air traffic controllers.Also Read| Trump rules out cyberattack, AI as US probes nationwide flight disruption The ground stop prevented aircraft from taking off, but flights that were already airborne were allowed to continue to their destinations and land. Officials said they were assessing aircraft still in the air on a case-by-case basis.The nationwide suspension was the first since January 2023, when a malfunction in a key FAA computer system disrupted flight operations. It was also only the second such order since the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Article Summary: Air India flights operating to and from the US could face disruptions after a communication outage forced the FAA to impose a nationwide ground stop on departures. The FAA said the decision was taken "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety" The ground stop has now been lifted according to Reuters, but the disruption is likely to continue.

As Chhath Puja celebrations continues till November 16, people planning bank visits around the festival may want to check the holiday calendar before heading out. While bank branches in some cities will remain closed on Monday on account of Chhath, the holiday is not applicable nationwide, with closures varying across states and cities.According to the Reserve Bank of India 's (RBI) November holiday calendar, banks in Patna and Ranchi will remain closed on Monday, November 16 for Chhath Puja. Branches in cities such as New Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata will remain open on the day.Chhath Puja is being observed over four days, from November 13 to 16 this year. The celebrations began with Nahay Khay, followed by Kharna on November 14. Devotees observed Sandhya Arghya on November 15, while the festival concludes on November 16 with Usha Arghya, when offerings are made to the rising Sun.Apart from Chhath Puja, banks will observe several regional holidays during the remainder of November. These closures vary across cities and states.Apart from regional and festival-specific holidays, bank branches across India remain closed on all Sundays and on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month.In November, the Sunday holidays fall on November 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29. Banks were also closed on November 14, the second Saturday, and will remain closed on November 28, the fourth Saturday.Customers should note that bank holidays apply to physical branches. Digital banking services, including UPI, mobile and internet banking, and ATMs are generally available on holidays.State-wise list of holidays in November[Source: RBI]

Article Title: India-Egypt trade has 'sky's the limit' potential, says Piyush Goyal; eyes bigger investments
Article Text:
File photo

India widens its trade network

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India and Egypt need to set their sights on a much bigger trade partnership, with greater two-way movement of goods, services and investments, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, calling for exploring new business opportunities between the two countries.With bilateral trade currently at around $6.5 billion, Goyal said the existing numbers did not reflect the potential of the two economies. He was speaking at a community event hosted by the Indian Community Association in Egypt (ICAE) late last evening."For the size of our two economies, I believe it's just a beginning; it cannot be our destination; the sky's the limit," he said.India is looking beyond selling its products in the Egyptian market and wants to attract Egyptian goods and investments as well. Goyal said both countries needed to identify areas where they could benefit from each other's strengths, making trade a two-way exercise."We are looking at investment opportunities in Egypt; we are looking at marketing our goods and services...we are looking at Egyptian products coming to India and investments coming to India in areas of Egypt's strength, because ultimately trade has to be two-way. It has to be a win-win between the two nations," he said.The trade figures for 2025-26 show India's exports to Egypt at $3.87 billion, against imports of $2.60 billion. Meat and poultry products, petroleum products, organic chemicals, cotton and machinery are among India's main exports to the country. Crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products account for its major imports.Investment flows, however, remain limited. India received just $11.5 million in foreign direct investment from Egypt between April 2000 and June 2026.Goyal is visiting Egypt for two days with a 132-member business delegation. His schedule includes meetings with Egyptian leaders and business representatives to explore ways of increasing trade and investment between the two countries.Goyal also outlined India's broader approach to international trade, saying the government had placed it at the heart of the country's economic agenda. The focus, he said, was on opening up markets and securing preferential access for Indian goods and services, particularly in countries with which India has friendly relations."We are opening the doors for greater competition with the world, opening the doors of markets across the world for preferential access for Indian goods and services, particularly with our friendly countries. Towards that end, we have expanded our free trade agreements to many more developed nations," he added.India has implemented trade agreements with Mauritius, Australia, the UAE, Oman, the EFTA bloc, New Zealand and the UK over the past five years. An agreement with the European Union is scheduled to be signed next month.Negotiations are also under way with Canada, Chile, the South Africa-led South African Customs Union (SACU), the Brazil-led Mercosur grouping and the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).Following these agreements, Indian goods will have preferential access to markets representing $85 trillion of the global GDP of $115 trillion.Looking to make it easier for companies in both countries to identify and pursue opportunities, Goyal proposed that the ICAE put together a business guide for Indian and Egyptian enterprises."Maybe you need to create a new 'Periplus' for businesses to engage between India and Egypt," he said.Periplus refers to an ancient guidebook or account of sea routes and trading ports.
Article Summary: India and Egypt need to set their sights on a much bigger trade partnership, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal says. Bilateral trade currently at around $6.5 billion. India is looking beyond selling its products in the Egyptian market and wants to attract Egyptian goods and investments.

Article Title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang exited company in 2025, stays silent on 'personal matters'
Article Text:
File photo: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang

Who is Alice Huang?

Megaspeed under scrutiny over Nvidia chips

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has confirmed that Alice Huang, the former executive at the centre of the controversy involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang, left the company in August 2025.The company told CNBC on Sunday that Alice Huang officially departed on August 30, 2025, and no longer holds any role there. It declined to comment on her personal affairs.“Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters,” the company said in an emailed statement.The announcement comes amid heightened scrutiny of Megaspeed following reports about Alice Huang's alleged relationship with Jensen Huang and her business connections in China. The New York Times has reported that US intelligence officials believe she was recruited by China's intelligence services to gather information on the Nvidia chief.Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife amid the reports and resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12. The reports also raised questions about another alleged relationship involving a senior Nvidia employee.Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, built a career in Chinese finance before moving into the artificial intelligence and cloud computing sector.She reportedly worked in television journalism before taking up roles in banking and investment management, including at HSBC's private banking arm in Hong Kong and Chinese investment bank CITIC Securities.She later held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm, where she was identified in company records as a deputy general manager and executive director. She became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to corporate records reviewed by research group C4ADS.Her business interests have also drawn attention because of reported links to Huawei. An investigation by private intelligence firm Tesari, shared with CNBC, found that Shanghai Hexi acquired a 27% stake in data centre developer Shanghai Century Longteng in 2021. Century Longteng held a controlling stake in Shenzhen Yifeng Technology, whose key customer was Huawei Cloud. Hexi exited its investment in Century Longteng in 2024.The findings establish an indirect business connection to infrastructure serving Huawei, but do not establish that the facility acquired Nvidia chips or that Alice Huang was involved in any unauthorised transfer of technology.Megaspeed describes itself as a core regional business partner of Nvidia's cloud computing business. It allows customers to rent computing capacity powered by Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), specialised chips used for complex computing tasks.The company, which operates in Singapore and Indonesia, has previously faced media and government scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia chips supplied through its business may have been redirected to customers in China.Megaspeed rejected allegations concerning its business, supply chain and global operations, saying the media reports were not supported by verifiable evidence. It said it had appointed external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.The company added that its operational and supply-chain controls were designed to comply with applicable laws, including US export control requirements and regulations in the markets where it operates.It said it would review the reports and communicate further with stakeholders as appropriate.
Article Summary: Megaspeed confirms Alice Huang officially departed on August 30, 2025. Company declined to comment on her personal affairs. Announcement comes amid heightened scrutiny of Megaspeed following reports about Alice Huang's alleged relationship with Jensen Huang. US intelligence officials believe she was recruited by China's intelligence services to gather information on the Nvidia chief.

Article Title: Tata Steel eyes NINL merger this fiscal; Rs 40,000 crore expansion awaits clearance
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger within the current financial year, with the final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) now awaited."The amalgamation of NINL with Tata Steel remains on track for completion this financial year," Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tata Steel, said.The NCLT is scheduled to hear the matter later this month. Its final approval will pave the way for Tata Steel's proposed Rs 40,000 crore expansion at the NINL facility.Tata Steel acquired NINL's assets for Rs 12,100 crore through its erstwhile subsidiary, Tata Steel Long Products (TSLP). The acquisition was completed in July 2022 and included a steel manufacturing unit with an annual production capacity of 1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).The company plans to add around 5 million tonnes of capacity to the facility, which is located about 5-10 km from its Kalinganagar steel plant. The proposed investment is part of Tata Steel's long products expansion plans in the region."We have... announced another 5 million tonne expansion in Neelachal (Ispat Nigam), which is also in Kalinganagar. It is a long products expansion, and we have announced that it is a Rs 40,000 crore project," Tata Steel CEO and Managing Director T V Narendran recently told PTI.NINL was the first state-owned steel company to be privatised by the Centre. Tata Steel is among the top global steelmakers, with an annual crude steel capacity of 36 million tonnes.
Article Summary: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger. The final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) is now awaited. Tata Steel acquired NINL's assets for Rs 12,100 crore through its erstwhile subsidiary, Tata Steel Long Products (TSLP)

Article Title: Sebi plans AI guardrails for capital markets, stresses human oversight in critical decisions
Article Text:
The proposed guidelines will set safeguards for AI use in capital markets, with disclosures, accountability and human oversight at their core.

Sebi reviews listing framework for startups

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, with a focus on investor protection, accountability and human oversight, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Sunday.The proposed guidelines will lay down safeguards for AI applications used by market participants, including disclosure requirements and accountability of regulated entities. A 'human-in-the-loop' approach will also ensure that critical decisions involving AI remain subject to human oversight, Pandey said, according to PTI.The regulator had floated a consultation paper in June 2025 proposing guiding principles for the responsible use of AI and machine learning in the securities market. The proposed framework aims to harness the benefits of the technology while addressing risks to investor protection, market integrity and financial stability.Pandey was speaking at the inauguration of Sebi's pavilion, titled 'Bharat Ka Share Bazaar', at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The pavilion, inaugurated on November 14, has been set up in association with market institutions, including the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL), National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) and the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).The pavilion features an AI zone and an Investor Facilitation Camp, where visitors can interact with officials and learn about safe investment practices. It also aims to educate people about fraudulent investment schemes, unregistered entities and illegal mobilisation of funds.Pandey urged participating institutions to use their interactions with visitors to identify processes that could be simplified and services that could be improved. He also highlighted Sebi's 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' campaign under Project Jagrook and reiterated the message 'Check, Validate and Verify', asking investors to understand an investment, verify its authenticity and assess its risks before committing money.The regulator has also been strengthening its cybersecurity framework amid rising threats to financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers. Sebi introduced a structured incident response mechanism in May, aligned with the Financial Stability Board's FIRE reporting template, Pandey said, reported ANI.On risks linked to quantum computing, the Sebi chief said the regulator was taking stock of cryptographic systems and identifying areas where the technology is used to assess potential vulnerabilities. Such risks could become more pronounced around 2032-35, making it important for markets to prepare in advance.Sebi has also developed supervisory tools, including 'Sudarshan', which is being showcased at international regulatory forums, and is working to strengthen its AI capabilities through global initiatives and supervisory toolkits.Pandey also said Sebi has set up a working group to examine ways to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive to startups, particularly deep-tech and biotech firms that may take longer to become profitable.The existing platform has not gained the desired traction, and the regulator is considering changes that could help such companies access public markets at an earlier stage. The aim is to give investors a clearer understanding of the higher risks involved while allowing them to participate in the companies' long-term growth potential.The 45th IITF, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, is being held at Bharat Mandapam from November 14 to 27. This year's theme is 'Vikas aur Virasat'.
Article Summary: The proposed guidelines will lay down safeguards for AI applications used by market participants, including disclosure requirements and accountability of regulated entities. A 'human-in-the-loop' approach will also ensure that critical decisions involving AI remain subject to human oversight. Sebi has also been strengthening its cybersecurity framework amid rising threats to financial institutions.

Article Title: Bad air, bigger bills: Air pollution drives health insurance claims up fourfold in 3 years
Article Text:
Pollution-related health insurance claims in India have risen 4.3 times in three years

Working professionals make up 59% of claims

Delhi leads, but smaller cities are not far behind

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Total claim amount rises 4.5 times

NEW DELHI: Pollution is not just leaving people gasping for breath but also burning a bigger hole in their health insurance bills. Claims linked to pollution have surged more than fourfold in just three years, with working professionals bearing the biggest brunt, accounting for nearly six out of every 10 such claims, according to data released by insurance aggregator Policybazaar.The company's data showed that pollution-associated health insurance claims increased 4.34 times between FY23 and FY26. The rise was steady over the three years, with claims jumping 67% in FY24, another 70% in FY25 and 53% in FY26.Rohan Goel, Business Head, Health Insurance at Policybazaar, said, "India's rising pollution levels are increasingly reflected in its healthcare burden. Our health insurance data shows that pollution-associated claims have surged 4.3 times."Interestingly, respiratory illnesses were not the only major contributor to these claims. Cardiovascular conditions accounted for the largest share at 43.5%, while other respiratory infections made up 35%.Pneumonia accounted for 11.2% of claims, followed by bronchitis at 6%.The 31-55 age group accounted for the largest portion of pollution-associated health insurance claims, at 59%. Senior citizens aged 55 and above were the second-largest group, contributing 31%.The remaining claims came from younger age groups. Young adults aged 21-30 accounted for 6.7%, while children below 20 years made up 3.7%.Goel said, "Working professionals aged 31-55 account for nearly 59% of claims, while senior citizens contribute another 31%."Delhi recorded the highest number of pollution-associated health insurance claims among cities. Pune, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Hyderabad followed.However, the numbers were not concentrated only in major cities. Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities together accounted for 55% of the claims, showing that the trend extended beyond metropolitan centres.The timing of these claims also followed a seasonal pattern. In FY26, nearly 56% of all annual pollution-associated health insurance claims were recorded beween October and March, when air pollution levels typically worsen across several parts of the country.The increase in claims also came with a sharp rise in the overall amount paid out. Policybazaar's data showed that the total claim amount increased 4.5 times between FY23 and FY26. The average claim amount, meanwhile, continued to remain above FY23 levels.The data further showed that 48% of consumers living in highly polluted cities opted for higher health insurance coverage.Goel said, "These trends highlight the growing importance of preventive healthcare, timely medical attention and adequate health insurance coverage to manage the financial impact of unexpected medical needs."
Article Summary: Pollution-related health insurance claims in India have risen 4.3 times in three years. Working professionals make up 59% of claims. Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities together accounted for 55% of the claims. 48% of consumers living in highly polluted cities opted for higher health insurance coverage.

Article Title: FPIs pump Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities in November after two months of outflows
Article Text:
The latest inflows follow net withdrawals of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September

Why are foreign investors returning to Indian markets?

What should investors watch next?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) returned to Indian equities in November, pumping in Rs 84,290 crore in the first 13 days of the month after two consecutive months of net selling. The sharp reversal in foreign flows comes amid a global sell-off in artificial intelligence-linked stocks, falling crude oil prices and renewed interest in select large-cap Indian shares.FPIs made net investments during nine trading sessions between November 2 and 13, according to data from depositories. The latest buying has also narrowed their cumulative net withdrawals from Indian equities in 2026 to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore, from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago.The return of foreign money follows net outflows of Rs 35,861 crore in September and Rs 34,843 crore in October, reflecting the pressure Indian equities faced from overseas investors in the preceding months.However, market experts caution that the latest buying may not signal a sustained return of foreign investors."November's foreign buying is a sharp tactical turn, not yet a structural return. Falling crude and money rotating out of the crowded Asian AI trade have pushed FPIs to close an extreme underweight on India, and most of that buying has gone into index heavyweights," said Vedant Gupte, co-founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk, as quoted by PTI.He added that foreign investors had recovered only a small portion of their withdrawals this year, while domestic institutional investors were using the market rally to book profits.Foreign portfolio investors are overseas individuals, institutions or funds that invest in financial assets such as shares and bonds in another country. Unlike foreign direct investors, they generally do not seek management control of the companies they invest in. Their buying and selling activity can influence stock prices, market liquidity and the flow of foreign capital into an economy.The sell-off in global AI-linked stocks has encouraged investors to look beyond technology-heavy markets and explore opportunities elsewhere, said Rohan Goyal, investment research analyst at MIRA Money.A decline in crude oil prices has also improved the investment outlook for India, which imports a large share of its oil requirements. Brent crude fell around 13 per cent in the first week of November to nearly $97 per barrel. Easing geopolitical concerns, attractive valuations in select large-cap stocks and better visibility on domestic corporate earnings have further supported foreign buying, Goyal said.The inflows have helped the benchmark Nifty cross the 25,000-mark. Financials, telecom, capital goods, pharmaceuticals and automobile stocks have seen strong buying, while some power-related shares have gained on the back of robust earnings, said VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments.He also attributed part of the market rally to short-covering in frontline large-cap stocks, particularly select leading banking shares.The direction of foreign flows and the sustainability of the market rally will depend on several domestic and global factors. Markets will track minutes of the US Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting, crude oil prices amid tensions involving Iran and Gulf countries, movements in the rupee and expectations around a possible RBI rate hike next week.The remaining second-quarter corporate earnings announcements, broader market participation and the Nifty's ability to hold above 25,000 will also influence sentiment. Developments in the global unwinding of the AI trade will remain another key factor, said Dheeraj Gaur, chief investment strategy officer at Choice Wealth.In the debt market, foreign investors invested Rs 7,815 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and Rs 1,167 crore through the general route. They withdrew Rs 702 crore through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR).
Article Summary: FPIs made net investments during nine trading sessions between November 2 and 13. The latest buying has narrowed their cumulative net withdrawals from Indian equities in 2026 to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore. Financials, telecom, capital goods, pharmaceuticals and automobile stocks have seen strong buying, while some power-related shares have gained.

Article Title: Govt tightens procurement rules, mandates scrutiny of bids 30% below estimated cost
Article Text:
The move aims to prevent unusually low quotes from compromising the quality and timely execution of government projects.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The finance ministry has directed government agencies to scrutinise bids quoting prices more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost of a project or contract, tightening checks on unusually low offers to prevent compromises in quality and timely execution.The department of expenditure has defined such offers as Abnormally Low Bids (ALBs) and made it mandatory for procuring entities to examine them as potentially unviable. Agencies will have to seek written explanations from bidders when concerns arise over their ability to deliver the work at the quoted price."A bid quoting a price more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost shall mandatorily be examined as a potentially ALB," the department said in an office memorandum, as quoted by PTI.The bidder may be asked to provide a detailed price analysis in relation to the scope of work specified in the tender document. The procuring agency will assess whether the quoted amount is sufficient to meet the contract requirements.However, the new threshold does not mean that every bid priced more than 30 per cent below the estimate will be rejected. The department clarified that the threshold would not be grounds for "automatic rejection" and that bidders would be given an opportunity to explain how they intend to execute the contract at the offered price.A bid may be rejected if the bidder fails to adequately demonstrate its ability to complete the work at the quoted rate. In such cases, the agency can consider the next higher bidder, provided its price is found reasonable.The move addresses a gap in earlier procurement rules, which did not prescribe a fixed numerical threshold for identifying abnormally low bids. Government agencies largely relied on their own assessment of whether an unusually low quotation posed a risk to the execution of a contract.The department has also advised procuring entities to frame tender specifications carefully to guard against such bids. The revised framework is intended to bring greater uniformity and transparency to the process while allowing genuine price competition.Government agencies invite bids from companies and contractors through a tender process to procure goods, services or carry out projects. Interested bidders submit their technical proposals and price quotations, which are evaluated against the conditions specified in the tender. While a lower price can make a bid more competitive, an unusually low quote may raise questions about whether the bidder can meet the required quality standards and complete the contract within the agreed cost.
Article Summary: The finance ministry has directed government agencies to scrutinise bids quoting prices more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost of a project or contract. The department of expenditure has defined such offers as Abnormally Low Bids (ALBs) The move aims to prevent unusually low quotes from compromising the quality and timely execution of government projects.

Article Title: 76-year-old with Rs 35 lakh health cover denied Rs 3.87 lakh claim over wrong kidney disease entry corrected during admission; panel orders payout, 6% interest, Rs 50,000 compensation and Rs 35,000 co
Article Text:
According to the woman, she had disclosed her existing medical conditions, including diabetes, lipid disorders and hypertension, while obtaining the policies. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why the court ruled in favour of the woman

Manmohan Nanda v. United India Assurance Co. Ltd.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

You have health insurance policies, but when you are hospitalised a wrong ailment is erroneously recorded in your charts, which the hospital later rectifies. But the insurance company rejects your claim for non-submission of mandatory documents, even though medical records had clarified the erroneous reference during the hospital admission. What do you do?In one such case, a 76-year-old woman had to pay Rs 3.87 lakh for her hospital treatment despite holding health insurance policies with a combined sum insured of Rs 35 lakh.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-VIII (Central), Delhi, held Nthe insurance company guilty of deficiency in service over its handling of the claim.In its order dated September 24, 2026, the commission found that the insurer continued to seek medical clarification despite records showing that the erroneous entry had been corrected during the same hospital admission.A woman held two health insurance policies - the first provided a sum insured of Rs 10 lakh against a premium of Rs 96,673. The second carried a sum insured of Rs 25 lakh and involved an additional premium of Rs 54,499.According to the woman, she had disclosed her existing medical conditions, including diabetes, lipid disorders and hypertension, while obtaining the policies. She also stated that the insurer had conducted a pre-policy medical examination, whose report did not record any pre-existing disease relating to her heart or kidneys.In December 2023, she was admitted to the emergency department of a hospital in Delhi. The initial emergency assessment inadvertently recorded chronic kidney disease (CKD). The woman maintained that this entry was erroneous and was corrected through an addendum, before she was discharged.During her hospitalisation, a cashless claim request was submitted to the insurance company. The insurer sought additional medical records, investigation reports and clarifications. The woman stated that she supplied the requested information, including a treating doctor's certificate indicating that she had no history of CKD or coronary artery disease.The cashless request was nevertheless not approved, with the reason communicated being insufficiency or non-submission of the requisite documents. After being discharged, she paid the hospital bill of Rs 3.8 lakh herself and subsequently filed a reimbursement claim.The insurer acknowledged the reimbursement claim in January 2024, and sought hard copies of the original documents. It continued to request information over the following weeks. In February, it confirmed receipt of the physical documents and informed her that the claim was under hospital-level verification.Towards March-end, the insurer again sought an affidavit from the treating doctor confirming that there was no history of CKD.The woman argued that this was unnecessary because the hospital had already clarified the erroneous entry through the addendum and a medical certificate. According to her complaint, the treating doctor also explained that a separate affidavit from the emergency doctor would not be provided because the error had already been corrected in the medical record.The insurance company rejected the reimbursement claim by email in April 2024, citing non-submission of mandatory documents.The woman then approached the consumer commission, seeking reimbursement, interest, compensation and litigation expenses.The insurer did not file its written version within the statutory period. By an order dated May 29, 2025, the commission closed its right to file the written version and evidence. It subsequently considered the insurer's written arguments only on questions of law, not disputed factual matters that should have been presented through its written version and evidence.The commission examined the medical records and correspondence between the parties, focusing on whether the insurer had acted reasonably in processing and rejecting the claim.It noted that the initial emergency assessment mentioned CKD, but the addendum correcting the entry had been issued during the same hospital admission. The treating doctor's clarification and other records were also available to the insurer.The commission observed: “The significance of the correction is that the alleged discrepancy was not discovered for the first time after the claim had been raised.”It further noted that the insurer had been informed about the correction and had received the treating doctor's clarification, yet continued to seek an affidavit addressing the same issue.The commission recognised that insurers can request documents to verify claims. However, it held that this right cannot justify repeated demands for material already supplied or documents that cannot reasonably be obtained in the circumstances.As the order stated: “However, such right cannot be exercised in a manner whereby the insured is repeatedly called upon to furnish documents which have already been supplied or documents which, in the circumstances, are not reasonably capable of being obtained.”The commission also observed that the insurer had not produced evidence establishing what essential information remained unavailable after the medical documents and clarifications had been furnished.Its February communication, confirming that the case was under hospital-level verification, indicated that the claim was being processed on the basis of the submitted documents.The order said: “In these circumstances, the subsequent rejection of the claim merely on the ground of non-submission of further documents, without satisfactorily establishing why the documents already supplied were insufficient for adjudication, amounts to an unreasonable handling of the insurance claim.”The commission also referred to the Supreme Court's decision in, noting the principle that an insurer that conducts a pre-policy medical assessment must assess the medical risk on the information available to it.Concluding that the claim had not been processed and decided fairly, reasonably and diligently, the commission held that the insurance company had committed deficiency in service.It stated: “The Commission is therefore of the considered view that the Opposite Party failed to process and decide the complainant’s claim in a fair, reasonable and diligent manner and thereby committed deficiency in service.”The commission directed the insurance company to pay the reimbursement amount, interest, compensation and litigation costs within 45 days of receiving the order.The commission directed the insurer to reimburse the hospital expenses of Rs 3,87,391, pay interest at 6% per annum from April 25, 2024, until realisation, and provide Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental agony, harassment and inconvenience. It also awarded Rs 35,000 towards litigation expenses.If it failed to comply with the monetary directions within that period, the principal reimbursement amount would carry interest at 9% per annum instead of 6%, calculated from April 25, 2024, until actual realisation.
Article Summary: A 76-year-old woman had to pay Rs 3.87 lakh for her hospital treatment despite holding health insurance policies with a combined sum insured of Rs 35 lakh. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-VIII (Central), Delhi, held Nthe insurance company guilty of deficiency in service over its handling of the claim.

Article Title: AI losing its shine? Why global investors could turn to India for their next big bet
Article Text:
Why global investors could turn to India for their next big bet

Foreign investors bring money back to Dalal Street

Machinery imports signal pickup in private investment

Why the AI investment story is facing questions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As investors begin to question whether the AI frenzy is worth the money being poured into it, India could emerge as an attractive destination for global funds. Heavy AI spending by US technology companies and concerns over returns may encourage fund managers to scout for opportunities beyond technology stocks, according to Jefferies.India could be among the biggest beneficiaries of this shift, the brokerage said in its latest GREED & fear investment strategy report."In emerging markets which GREED & fear knows more about, the obvious market to benefit from the reverse AI trade has been India."The report said more fund managers were now looking at investment options outside AI stocks, as doubts grow over whether the AI boom can continue."From an investment standpoint, the now widespread view that the AI thematic has peaked is leading to a growing desire to look at non-AI trades on the part of portfolio managers."Signs of this shift are already visible in foreign investment flows into Indian equities. Overseas investors have bought a net $7.2 billion worth of shares over three weeks, including a record $5.2 billion in the week ended November 6, Jefferies said.The buying comes after a period of heavy foreign selling. Net outflows from Indian equities stood at $32.4 billion since the beginning of 2026 and $51.2 billion since the beginning of 2025, measured over the respective periods.Jefferies said India's relatively attractive stock valuations and better-than-expected economic recovery were adding to its appeal."The other point about India is that valuations, relative to history, remain comparatively modest while the cyclical recovery in the economy this year has been better than expected."The Nifty was trading at 18.4 times its expected earnings over the next year, while the Nifty MidCap 100 was trading at 23.1 times its expected earnings.The report also highlighted signs that private-sector investment is picking up. Machinery imports, an indicator of investment activity, more than doubled from $29 billion in FY21 to $62 billion in FY26. They rose further to $67 billion in the 12 months ending September 2026.Domestic investors have also continued to support the market through mutual fund investments. Equity mutual fund inflows stood at Rs 350 billion in October, taking the total for the first ten months of 2026 to Rs 3.9 trillion."India remains the most dynamic capital market in the world after the US," Jefferies said. However, the brokerage noted that the growing supply of equities had limited gains in benchmark indices.The possible shift towards markets such as India comes as investors increasingly question the returns that large US technology companies are getting from their heavy AI spending.Jefferies said the median forecast return on invested capital for four major US technology companies had fallen from 21.7 per cent to 16.8 per cent for 2027. This decline comes even as their capital spending is expected to increase.The brokerage believes that growing concerns over AI investment returns could encourage global fund managers to diversify into other markets. India could benefit from this shift, backed by improving private-sector investment activity and continued inflows into domestic equity mutual funds.
Article Summary: Jefferies says more fund managers are looking at investment options outside AI stocks. Overseas investors have bought a net $7.2 billion worth of shares over three weeks. Machinery imports more than doubled from $29 billion to $62 billion in FY26.

Article Title: India's life insurance sector set for 13-18% annual growth in premiums through FY29: Report
Article Text:
Representative image

Protection and annuity products drive growth

Higher expenses and mixed persistency trends remain concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's life insurance sector is expected to maintain healthy growth over the next three years, supported by rising demand for protection products, stronger traction in annuity and non-participating savings policies, and improving profitability, according to a research report by Centrum Broking.The brokerage expects private life insurers to record an annualised premium equivalent (APE) compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13-18% between FY26 and FY29, reflecting continued demand for insurance products and a gradual improvement in business mix.“We continue to remain optimistic on life insurance industry with a healthy Q2,” the report said, identifying a shift towards more profitable products and expanding value of new business (VNB) margins as key factors supporting the outlook.During the second quarter of FY27, APE growth among insurers ranged from 7% to 16%, while gross premium growth for private insurers stood at 8-16% year-on-year, according to the report.New business premium growth also remained encouraging, with insurers reporting increased traction in both individual and group insurance segments.One of the key trends highlighted by the brokerage was the industry's shift towards protection, non-participating savings and annuity products.Insurers have been reducing their dependence on unit-linked insurance plans (ULIPs), which are exposed to market fluctuations, while focusing on products that offer more stable margins and profitability.“Overall, annuity is emerging as a key growth driver, supported by demand for guaranteed returns and retirement solutions, while insurers increasingly shift towards protection and higher-margin products,” the report said.The changing product mix has also supported an improvement in VNB margins, which measure the profitability of new insurance business.During the first half of FY27, VNB margins expanded by 10-170 basis points year-on-year across private insurers. The report attributed the improvement to stronger protection business, a favourable product mix and operating leverage.Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) also recorded a 470-basis-point expansion in its VNB margin to 22.3%.Despite the growth in premiums and profitability, insurers continue to face operational challenges.Expense ratios increased across several private insurers in the second quarter of FY27, primarily because of higher operating costs. Persistency trends, which indicate the proportion of policies that remain active over time, were also mixed, with 13-month persistency declining across most insurers.On the regulatory front, insurers expressed confidence in their ability to comply with proposed norms. However, further clarity is expected after the final regulations are released.Centrum Broking said sustained growth in protection products and annuity offerings, along with expansion of distribution networks, would remain important drivers of the sector's business growth and profitability over the coming years.
Article Summary: India's life insurance sector is expected to maintain healthy growth over the next three years. Rising demand for protection products, stronger traction in annuity and non-participating savings policies, and improving profitability are key factors supporting the outlook.Higher expenses and mixed persistency trends remain concerns.

Article Title: Online platforms liable for banned listings: Panel
Article Text:
AI-generated image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law and must exercise due diligence before allowing listings of prohibited, hazardous and regulated products, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has ruled.The order will have wider implications and act as a deterrent to the sale of hazardous items such as explosives, acids and jammers that pose a danger, as well as other regulated products. Online platforms and e-commerce companies often cite their intermediary status to escape responsibility and action in such cases.The NCDRC passed the order while hearing appeals filed by Weblink.in against two orders of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) concerning the online listing of ammonium nitrate, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate. The authority had imposed a penalty of Rs 20 lakh on the platform in the two cases.The commission upheld the penalty imposed by the authority. In its order passed earlier this week, the commission said the platform could not claim immunity under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act on the ground that it had no “actual knowledge” of the listings. It also said the company could not plead “selective diligence”.In one of the orders, the commission said, “The platform has its own list of do’s and don’ts, and it is evident they are not unaware of the precautions while facilitating transactions through their platforms in respect of hazardous substances or such prohibited items detrimental to the life of consumers. The argument that they are not obliged to verify licences as there is no such statutory obligation deserves rejection as the platform has the obligation to take reasonable care and exercise due diligence while allowing its platform to be utilised for such advertisement. ..”
Article Summary: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) passed the order while hearing appeals filed by Weblink.in against two orders of the Central Consumer Protection Authority.

Article Title: US trade deal talks near finishing line: EAM
Article Text:
EAM S Jaishankar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar Saturday said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were "not so much at our end" and that negotiations are near the "finishing line"."Well, it's certainly our hope, and in many ways anticipation that we are at the last stretch," he said.The comments come a week after a team of US officials came to India to discuss the customs and trade facilitation chapter with India, which is waiting for clarity on what the new tariff framework will be after the US Supreme Court ruled that US President Donald Trump's "reciprocal tariffs" were illegal. His comments may be an indication that govt is awaiting the next step from the Trump administration - which is conducting a second Section 301 probe against over a dozen countries for structural overcapacity.For several weeks now, officials from both sides have been stating that talks are in the final lap, with Trump also saying the deal with India may be different from other deals. "For us, the key is that we want a trade deal which is beneficial, is balanced and which would give us a comparative advantage over groups of comparable economies," Jaishankar said at the HT Leadership Summit.The repeated comments have raised hopes of the first tranche of the deal being announced soon, although things can move only after the US Trade Representative completes the second probe.PM Modi and Trump are due to meet in the US next month.Jaishankar said the US is India's biggest market and having the trade deal with it would benefit the country. "For the US, Trump is obviously looking to do a whole set of bilateral deals to improve markets for himself. Now, the challenge is to find a landing point.""I think this is not something which could have been done quickly, because these are serious issues; people's jobs and people's lives are at stake."
Article Summary: S Jaishankar said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were "not so much at our end" The comments come a week after a team of US officials came to India to discuss the customs and trade facilitation chapter with India.

Article Title: Strong economy drives NH toll to record 6,640cr in Oct
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Toll collection on national highways and expressways touched an all-time high of around Rs 6,640 crore in Oct, indicating stronger economic activity and increased movement of vehicles across the country's highway network.The collection of user fee was around 16% higher than the Rs 5,715 crore recorded in Oct 2025. The previous highest monthly toll revenue was Rs 6,185 crore, collected in May this year. Going by the trend, the total toll collection is projected to be around Rs 74,000 crore, officials said.A significant change was also visible in the mode of payment, with cash collections dropping sharply to barely Rs 4 crore last month from Rs 84 crore in the corresponding month last year. At the same time, payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) rose to around Rs 100 crore in Oct, against no such collection a year ago.The sharp decline in cash transactions follows govt directions to move away from cash payments for highway user fees and use FASTag or UPI as the default modes for paying the user charge. Officials said stricter monitoring was being carried out to ensure that cash is completely phased out as a mode of toll payment. "End of cash transaction will eliminate any scope of malpractices. More people are also opting for FASTag Annual Passes, which is a good sign," said another official. Growing adoption of electronic toll collection has reduced dependence on cash at toll plazas. The rise in UPI payments also indicates the gradual expansion of digital payment options for highway users.
Article Summary: Collection of user fee was around 16% higher than the Rs 5,715 crore recorded in Oct 2025. Cash collections dropped sharply to barely Rs 4 crore last month from Rs 84 crore in the corresponding month last year. At the same time, payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) rose to around Rs 100 crore in Oct.

Article Title: Sen-sational turnaround: Lakshya fights back from one game down to lift Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Lakshya Sen came from a game down to beat Japan's Koki Watanabe in the men's singles final and win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title in Kumamoto on Sunday.The world No. 13 lost the opening game but fought back to win the next two and seal a 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 victory in one hour and four minutes.Sen took control in the deciding game after opening up a 11-7 lead. He extended his advantage to nine points and did not allow Watanabe to fight his way back into the contest.The title comes shortly after Sen won the Hylo Open in Germany. His victory in Kumamoto also earned him 9,200 ranking points.Watanabe opened up a 3-0 lead, with Lakshya being a tad laid-back initially. The Japanese nailed his smashes to perfection, varying the pace. He repeatedly produced straight down-the-line smashes on Lakshya's forehand side to move to 6-1. Lakshya cut down the lead to 5-8.A judgement error and then a wide return made it 5-10. An angled smash from the Indian was followed by a net error as Watanabe took a five-point advantage into the break.On resumption, Lakshya fought his way back to 10-12, with the Indian producing a straight smash and a defensive block. Another superb return-to-serve helped him close the gap to 11-12.The Indian dived to save a point, only to send the shuttle long. Another shot going long took Watanabe to a 15-11 lead.Watanabe looked in control as he continued to find winners to establish a six-point lead at 18-12. The Japanese soon grabbed eight game points with another straight return. The Indian saved one before going wide.A change of sides brought a change of fortune as Lakshya surged to a 5-0 lead. The Indian took control of the net and didn't allow his opponent to find his way. He pounced on a loose net shot, and a net error from his opponent helped him maintain his 5-0 lead. A perfect cross-court smash earned him a five-point lead at the break.Despite a few errors, Lakshya's quick racquet speed helped him maintain his lead at 15-10. Watanabe also committed many errors, hitting wide and into the net, to leave the Indian three points away from forcing a decider.The Japanese fought back from 10-19 to make it 17-19, but Lakshya soon grabbed three game points with a fast push. He sent one shot long before unleashing another thunderous and precise smash to roar back into the contest.In the decider, a full-stretch dive to produce a defensive block gave Lakshya a 2-1 lead as the two played some fascinating rallies.The rallies got tighter and the score closer as the two battled hard to take control. From 3-3, Lakshya opened up a 9-6 lead before producing another pinpoint smash.The Indian took a four-point cushion at the interval after a push that seemed to be going wide managed to find its spot.Two brutal smashes extended Lakshya's lead to 13-7. Attack was the word as Lakshya kept producing attacking returns to leave his opponent dazed.Another steep winner to his opponent's backhand, followed by another lethal smash, took him to 16-7, leaving the local fans silent.From 7-17, Watanabe again fought back to 13-19 before Lakshya found two perfect returns to earn seven match points. He sealed the match on the second occasion with another cross-court winner.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen beats Koki Watanabe to win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title. The world No. 13 lost the opening game but fought back to win next two. Sen took control in the deciding game after opening up a 11-7 lead.

Article Title: Global economy to grow 2.8% in 2027 as AI spending, lower oil prices support outlook: Goldman Sachs
Article Text:
Representative image

Lower energy prices and AI spending to support growth

China growth outlook and risks to global economy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The global economy is expected to maintain steady growth in 2027, supported by declining energy prices and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI), although geopolitical tensions, fiscal pressures and uncertainty over technology spending could pose risks, according to a research report by Goldman Sachs.Global gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to expand by 2.8% in 2027, compared with an estimated 2.7% in 2026, said Jan Hatzius, chief economist and head of Goldman Sachs Research.The United States, Japan and the United Kingdom are expected to outperform consensus growth estimates, while South Korea and Taiwan are projected to benefit from continued strength in AI-related exports.“We expect another year of solid but unremarkable GDP growth in 2027, but several of the impulses that shaped global growth in 2026 will look different,” Hatzius said.A key factor behind the improved outlook is the expected moderation in energy prices. Goldman Sachs' commodity strategists expect Brent crude to fall to $78 per barrel by the end of 2027 as supply conditions in the Middle East normalise.The report said lower energy prices were expected to shift from being a drag on economic activity to providing modest support for global growth.AI investment is also expected to remain a significant contributor.Global nominal investment in AI is projected to rise to $1.8 trillion in 2027 from $1.1 trillion in 2026, driven largely by higher spending on hardware in the US.Goldman Sachs estimates that AI investment will add 0.4 percentage points to global GDP growth in 2027, with its contribution to US economic growth projected at 0.6 percentage points.“Even with the expected slowdown, the impact on GDP growth will be sizable,” Hatzius said.The scale of financing required for the AI infrastructure expansion has also come into focus. In a separate report, Goldman Sachs estimated that AI-related debt issuance across global syndicated credit markets had reached $687 billion year-to-date as of November 3.The report said the five major technology companies known as hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle — had issued $296 billion in debt year-to-date, exceeding the bank's full-year forecast of $250 billion.Their financing obligations extend beyond direct borrowing. Goldman Sachs estimated that the five companies had $1.7 trillion in lease commitments and another $1.9 trillion in unconditional purchase commitments, excluding leases. Of the latter, $685 billion was due by the end of 2027.The bank cautioned that these commitments represented an additional demand on companies' cash resources. It also said market saturation was emerging as a key constraint on further AI-related borrowing.Among major economies, China is forecast to grow by 4.5% in 2027, slightly above the consensus estimate of 4.4%. However, weak domestic consumption and continued weakness in the property sector are expected to constrain domestic demand.Goldman Sachs said risks to global growth remained tilted to the downside, identifying a renewed escalation in Iran, widening fiscal deficits and lower-than-expected AI capital expenditure as potential sources of pressure.Inflation is expected to moderate as energy prices decline, potentially giving central banks room to move towards monetary policy easing later in 2027.The bank's outlook therefore points to continued global expansion, with lower energy costs and AI spending providing support, while geopolitical developments, fiscal conditions and the scale of future technology investment remain important risks.
Article Summary: Lower energy prices and AI spending to support growth, says Goldman Sachs. Global gross domestic product is projected to expand by 2.8% in 2027. United States, Japan and the United Kingdom are expected to outperform consensus growth estimates. South Korea and Taiwan are projected to benefit from continued strength in AI-related exports.

Article Title: US diesel prices retreat, fall below $6 per gallon for first time in two months
Article Text:
US diesel prices have decreased to below $6 a gallon after record highs that persisted for two months

US diesel prices have falled below the $6 level for the first time in two months. It has eased some of the pressure on consumers, farmers and businesses following a sharp increase triggered by disruptions to global oil supplies.The national average retail price fell to $5.998 per gallon on Saturday, according to fuel price tracker GasBuddy, cited by Reuters. The decline comes after diesel touched an all-time high of $6.519 on September 22, with prices briefly crossing $10 per gallon in California.The surge had become a wider economic concern because diesel is central to the transportation and freight industry. Higher fuel costs pushed up expenses for businesses and farmers, while adding to inflationary pressures on households. Fuel prices also became a major political issue, contributing to voter dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump's Republicans ahead of this month's midterm elections, which saw Democrats sweep both houses of Congress.The earlier price rally was driven by supply disruptions linked to the US-Israeli war against Iran and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. Washington's efforts to contain the increase, including temporarily lifting federal taxes on red-dyed diesel, easing sanctions on Russian fuel and announcing an $8 billion support programme for farmers, offered limited relief.The latest retreat comes amid a combination of softer crude prices and seasonal changes in fuel consumption. Brent crude futures have dropped 18.5 per cent over the past two weeks, while demand for diesel typically weakens during autumn as travel slows and hurricane-related risks to Gulf Coast refineries decline.Refinery output is also recovering as scheduled maintenance is largely completed by November, Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis, said.The easing in fuel costs is not limited to diesel. Average US gasoline prices also fell below $4 per gallon this month for the first time since August 10, GasBuddy data showed.
Article Summary: The national average retail price fell to $5.998 per gallon on Saturday. The decline comes after diesel touched an all-time high of $6.519 on September 22. The surge had become a wider economic concern because diesel is central to the transportation and freight industry.

Article Title: Megaspeed Malaysian arm Speedmatrix under scanner

Kuala Lumpur: The spotlight is now on Malaysia as the fallout of the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs more companies and alleged South East Asia-based intermediaries. Fears of high-performance Nvidia chips finding their way to China through Malaysia, bypassing the US trade curbs, have swung the authorities here into action.Ministry of investment, trade and industry (MITI) has intensified the probe into Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, in collaboration with Royal Malaysian Customs Department.Malaysia's home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said on Saturday that police had opened an investigation paper as early as April 2025 on allegations that Malaysian subsidiaries were used to circumvent US export restrictions on Nvidia AI chips.In a statement on Friday, MITI said emphatically that "it has never cleared Singapore-based Megaspeed or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix.""Speedmatrix is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia. Any verification visits carried out by MITI at these facilities are part of its regular monitoring of the data center sector, and should not be taken to mean that a company has been cleared. Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate," MITI stated.So what prompted MITI to take this stance when only a few days ago minister Johari Abdul Ghani said govt has not opened a formal inquiry into Speedmatrix as there was no evidence the firm broke the law by renting data centre space and using GPUs locally?Two things unfolded: Megaspeed's claims that inspections by US and Malaysian officials found no foul play, implying the company stayed in line, and second, industry sources said, the realisation that Malaysia's recent pivot to AI hardware, chip design and a strong data centre hub could possibly be hit if a rules-based ecosystem was missing from the narrative.
